steps.text: Whisk flour and salt together in a large bowl. Cut in shortening until it resembles coarse crumbs.

Mix cold water, egg, and vinegar together in a separate bowl. Add to flour mixture and blend with a fork until a ball of dough forms. Divide into three equal balls; flatten each ball into a disk. Wrap disks in plastic wrap and refrigerate until ready to use.

raw_recipe.headline: No-Fail Pie Crust
raw_recipe.description: Need a no-fail pie crust? This easy recipe can help. Basic pantry items make enough dough for three perfect pie crusts. Use now, or freeze for later!
raw_recipe.name: No-Fail Pie Crust

review.reviewBody: I have used this recipe for years, but there is one little difference. I add a scant teaspoon of salt. It helps the taste of the crust.

I have used this recipe for 40 years and I am always asked to bring the pies for occassions. I use Crisco shortening, but I substitue part of shortening with softened real dairy unsalted butter because it tastes better than the flavored stuff. In addition, I use a circular zippered clear plastic case to roll the crust as thinly as I can without it losing its integrity. Wax paper works also, but the thinner crust bakes to perfection and helps the waistline. I also brush the crust with milk using a pastry brush. An unused chip brush for painting works also.

tasted good and was pretty easy to make and work with, however this one loves to shrink when you're blind baking the crust! remember to use pie weights or beans, or you'll end up with a sad small disk of dough at the bottom of your pie form like i did :D i made some more dough and put it on the edges and still got compliments on it and i'll be using the recipe again

I have used this recipe forever as did generations before. If you use too much flour during the rolling process it will fall apart so keep in mind. This goes with all crust recipes. Also measure the vinegar exactly and don't use pickling vinegar. Use room temp eggs. All important for success. Shortening is best not butter. Very tried and true recipe!!

I have used this pie crust recipe for years, and it never disappoints. When making g fruit pies, I add a couple tablespoons of sugar to the pie crust mixture. I then brush milk on the crust, and sprinkle on another couple of tablespoons of surgar as well. My pies are always popular.

I finally found the pie crust recipe for me! I substituted butter for half the shortening, and used a scant teaspoon of salt. Instead of cutting the fat in by hand, I used my food processor. Easy Peezy! So tasty, and flaky. Worth the effort over using store-bought crusts for sure. I’ll never go back.

This pie crust was perfect and simple. Only suggestion is not to use an extra large egg. I made pies at home with a large size egg and the crust turned out flaky and was perfect for slicing. When I used an extra large egg, it turned out too mushy and was not suitable for rolling out. One other suggestion is that I was able to roll out the dough (with the large size egg) between two sheets of waxed paper. Using the waxed paper prevents from having to flour the surface where you are rolling the dough, so dough does not get so tough or dry.

I made this recipe using gluten-free flour from Krusteaze(sp?). I used organic Spectrum vegetable shortening and a tad more salt than the recipe called for. I read the reviews that said the dough wasn't elastic or didn't roll out right. I didn't even try to roll this dough out because I had a (I thought) brilliant Idea! Since I was making a pumpkin and sweet potato pie that needed no top crust, I just took the dough, molded it into the bottom of my pie pans, covered with cling wrap, and refrigerated until I was ready to fill and bake. It was SO easy and really good! I recommend trying it this way.

I used one teaspoon of salt, 1 cup of butter instead of shortening, apple cider vinegar because I didn't have regular vinegar, and a big dash of allspice to give the crust some pizzaz. It was delicious and I don't normally like to eat pie crust. I will use this again to make meat pies -without the allspice.
So good! Easy, flaky. I divided in two for a 10” deep dish pumpkin pie or chicken pot pie. A family favorite.
My fourth time using this recipe, the key is to let the dough chill. One hour in the refrigerator doesn't seem sufficient, I do at least six hours chilled. The dough rolls out fine and tastes great.
My daughter has a soy allergy. I used 1/2 cup of butter and half cup of ricotta and it worked wonderful. Ease to handle. Finished with an egg wash over the top…Apple pie.
I've been using this recipe for years. It always yields a beautiful flaky crust perfect for both sweet and savory pies. I love to make a pot pie and a dessert pie with the full batch.
Made several times and you are right. No Fail!!

AMAZING!!! Found this recipe last minute in a pitch to make a pie crust for our pot pies. Usually we buy store bought crust and after going food shopping they were sold out. My daughter found this recipe, we gave it a try and loved it. It smelled really strong of vinegar. Best pot pie we ever made. So good and so easy! No more store bought pie crust. Making this recipe again.
I followed the recipe and please add sugar when you make this. Easy absolutely although falls apart
Used 1/2 c butter, 1/2 c shortening. Sorry, image very blurry. I’ve been using this recipe for all of my pies.

Very simple to make and came out super flaky. I even managed a pretty decent lattice. But, the pastry taste needs improvement. Next time I will add more salt and perhaps substitute some butter in. I have one disk of dough left and am considering sprinkling some salt on it before I roll it out.

I wish I would have read through the comments before adding the shortening as taste test reveals it has zero flavor. I have baked pies for 40 years and I should have consulted my recipe cards. I’d add just under a teaspoon if I could. I did add 1/4 cup flour as It felt too soft to work up. I’m glad many people had good results. I might powder up some salt and press a dusting into the crust as I roll it out.
No changes
